items.summary: the first trilateral round since February, with Witkoff and Kushner mediating and Europe briefed separately because Moscow refused to seat it at the table.
items.matters: a territorial trade and an Article 5-style guarantee are both on the draft agenda.
items.body: x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy with US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Kyiv, Ukraine, on September 6, 2026 [File: Valentyn Ogirenko/Reuters] By Al Jazeera Staff , AP and Reuters Published On 10 Nov 2026 10 Nov 2026 Negotiators from Russia and Ukraine are set to meet for peace talks brokered by the United States in Abu Dhabi, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy saying that recent gains on the battlefield had strengthened his country’s hand. The meeting in the capital of the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday will be the third round of talks there this year, following security consultations in January and February . The US side is led by US President Donald Trump’s envoys, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who have spearheaded Washington’s mediation. “Ukrainian forces are currently genuinely strengthening Ukraine’s negotiating position,” Zelenskyy said in his nightly video address on Monday. He said Russia was “suffering record losses”, a claim Moscow disputes, and urged Washington to persuade the Kremlin to end the war. Zelenskyy said General Mykhailo Drapatyi had presented a report on Ukraine’s military positions that pointed to heavy recent Russian losses, and that Ukraine’s long-range strikes on targets inside Russia, including oil facilities, were having an effect. In Washington, DC, Trump told reporters that he saw a “very strong inclination” towards ending the war and that both sides were “tired of fighting”. Trump had promised to end the war quickly when he took office in January 2025, but a settlement has remained elusive nearly five years after Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. A US official, briefing reporters on the condition of anonymity, said on Monday that both Russia and Ukraine had privately shown some flexibility on a possible exchange of territory. Security guarantees for Ukraine would be a central topic, the official said, including the possibility of a defence commitment modelled on Article 5 of NATO’s founding treaty. Ukraine wants Russia pushed back to the original border between the two countries, while Russian President Vladimir Putin wants to obtain all of the Donbas region. Russia occupies roughly 20 percent of Ukraine , including Crimea and parts of the eastern Donbas region. The Russian move has not been recognised by the international community, but Trump has previously urged Kyiv to cede territory for a deal to end the war. The US official said any territorial agreement would most likely come at the end of…

items.headline: Trump's own Gaza board says Israel is too slow as floods destroy shelters
items.summary: the Board of Peace called the flooding an immediate humanitarian emergency and told Israel its winterisation steps are insufficient, while the Israeli military said it had let in 8,200 trucks and 91,000 tents.
items.matters: the ceasefire's guarantors are now publicly pressuring their own side.
items.body: Heavy rain over the past two days has swept away tens of thousands of tents in the territory, where virtually the entire population has been displaced at least once, and killed at least five people, according to Hamas-led authorities in Gaza. The Board of Peace, tasked with implementation of an October 2025 US-brokered ceasefire announced between Israel and Hamas, said it had been warning Israel, which controls all entry into the territory, of the need to prepare both for the winter and seasonal flooding. Moments before the statement came out, the Israeli military said it had allowed more than 8,200 trucks to enter the Gaza Strip with supplies including 91,000 tents. The Board of Peace acknowledged steps being taken by Israel but said that they remain “insufficient”. “We call on the leadership of the current Government of Israel to act immediately to authorise and facilitate the entry of all necessary winterisation and humanitarian supplies,” it said. Israel has taken a biting tone against Hamas over the floods, saying the militant group should have invested in infrastructure instead of weaponry. “Hamas doesn’t get to escape responsibility every time it rains,” the Israeli foreign ministry posted Sunday on X. The Board of Peace also called on Hamas to abide by commitments under the ceasefire. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who is fighting for his political survival following tight elections last month, has vowed to kill anyone involved in Hamas’s Oct 7, 2023 attack, the deadliest day ever for…

items.headline: Nowy tantiem uderzy w ceny elektroniki

items.matters: koszt trafi w każdy zakup sprzętu, a nie w tantiemy samych twórców.
items.body: Opłata ma rekompensować twórcom kopiowanie ich dzieł. Chodzi o nośniki, za pośrednictwem których możemy słuchać piosenek, audiobooków, słuchowisk oraz oglądać filmy, seriale i bajki. Co ciekawe, na liście - obok dekoderów, pendrive'ów i kart - są też wymienione jako osobne pozycje komputery i dyski. Dla konsumentów oznacza to droższe zakupy przedświąteczne. Telefony komórkowe z wbudowaną pamięcią, smartfony (od 32 GB), tablety z wbudowaną pamięcią, komputery stacjonarne i przenośne, twarde zyski, w tym zewnętrzne, karty pamięci zewnętrznej, pendrive'y - te wszystkie urządzenia zostały rozporządzeniem z kwietnia tego roku dodane do listy urządzeń objętych opłatą reprograficzną. Jej wysokość będzie wynosiła 1 proc. sprzedaży netto, dzięki czemu do branży kreatywnej rocznie ma trafić od 150 do 200 mln zł. Do tej pory wpływy te były niskie i oscylowały wokół kwot 35-36 mln zł (dane za rok 2024). Stowarzyszenie Dziennikarzy i Wydawców Repropol zaznacza jednak, że szacunki resortu kultury są mocno orientacyjne i bazują na doświadczeniach innych państw Unii Europejskiej. Nie bez znaczenia jest też fakt, że opłata zacznie obowiązywać w okresie wzmożonych zakupów - zbliżających się wyprzedaży w związku z Black Friday, a także świąt Bożego Narodzenia, w związku z czym może się okazać, że prognozy wpływów są zawyżone. Wynika to bezpośrednio z tzw. efektu sezonowości i specyfiki handlu elektroniką. Czwarty kwartał tradycyjnie odpowiada za nieproporcjonalnie dużą część rocznej sprzedaży. Jeśli urzędnicy potraktują pierwsze, rekordowe wpływy z opłaty pobranej w okresie świątecznym jako rynkowy standard i proporcjonalnie przełożą je na kolejne miesiące, całoroczne szacunki okażą się zbyt optymistyczne (w pierwszej połowie roku popyt na sprzęt drastycznie spada). Dodatkowo, głębokie wyprzedaże obniżają końcową cenę netto urządzeń, a to właśnie od niej bezpośrednio naliczany jest 1-procentowy odpis. W efekcie realna kwota trafiająca do puli z pojedynczego urządzenia sprzedanego w promocji będzie niższa, niż zakładałby to model oparty na standardowych cenach katalogowych. Środowisko związane z branżą artystyczną od 12 lat apelowało o nowelizację przepisów w sprawie opłaty. Ostatni raz aktualizowano je w 2008 roku i są one bardzo anachroniczne, ponieważ obejmowały urządzenia, które wychodzą już z użytku, czyli magnetofony, magnetowidy, odtwarzacze MP3, ale i drukarki. Możliwość obciążenia tym dodatkowym kosztem producentów i importerów urządzeń elektronicznych daje ustawa Prawo autorskie. Dzięki zawartym tam regulacjom wystarczy, że minister wyda rozporządzenie o nowych…

Na dziś na godz. 10 wyznaczone zostało kolejne — już drugie — zwołane przez Annę Korwin-Piotrowską zgromadzenie sędziów w siedzibie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego . Celem zgromadzenia jest dokonanie zmian w Regulaminie Trybunału Konstytucyjnego. W stolicy Zjednoczonych Emiratów Arabskich Abu Zabi rozpoczynają się zaplanowane na dwa dni trójstronne rozmowy Ukraina-USA-Rosja. To pierwsze negocjacje w tym formacie od lutego. items.body: 宮野宏樹 Nov 10, 2026 10:04 Investigation into Mr. Huang Yesterday (November 9) was a day where the foundations supporting AI were shaken. Nvidia's stock price fell following the board's decision to launch an investigation into CEO Huang, Anthropic released new Claude models, and it was revealed they invested $3.4 billion in power generators. We have narrowed down the news to seven key stories, including Google's new chip, Mr. Trump's comments on regulation, and the growth of Chinese firms. On November 9, Nvidia's stock price closed down 4.27% (CNBC). This followed an announcement on the previous day, Sunday the 8th, that the company's board of directors would begin an independent investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. According to the announcement, the investigation will be conducted by a committee of independent directors with the assistance of an external law firm. The board stated that Mr. Huang had been a 'target of operations by foreign intelligence agencies.' The New York Times and Financial Times had reported that Mr. Huang was in a relationship with a woman whom U.S. intelligence authorities suspected of leaking information to the Chinese side. The board stated there is no reason to believe that national security or Nvidia's confidential information has been compromised, and that they trust Mr. Huang and the management team. Mr. Huang will remain CEO and says he will cooperate with the investigation. In an email to employees, he apologized for failing to fulfill his responsibilities. The Chinese Foreign Ministry has countered that the view of him being a spy is baseless. On this day, other semiconductor stocks rose significantly. AMD was up 13.26%, Marvell up 9.49%, and Broadcom up 8.78%. Only Nvidia saw a decline. Practical takeaway: Nvidia will announce its earnings on November 17. The immediate focus will be on the progress of the investigation and how the U.S. Congress and government decide to handle exports to China, rather than the financial results themselves. On November 9, Anthropic announced new versions of its top-tier models, 'Claude Fable 5.2' and 'Claude Mythos 5.2.' The two are the same model internally. Fable strengthens mechanisms to prevent dangerous uses such as cyberattacks and biological threats and is provided to all users. Mythos lacks these restrictions and is available only to organizations that have passed a vetting process. According to the company's announcement, output speed has increased by up to 30% compared to the previous version. The price is $8 per 1 million input tokens and $40 for output. items.body: .NET and .NET Core refer to several technologies including the runtime, the SDK, ASP.NET Core, and Entity Framework Core. Looking for the support policy for another part of the .NET platform? See the .NET Support Policy page. Every Microsoft product has a lifecycle. The lifecycle begins when a product is released and ends when it's no longer supported. Knowing key dates in this lifecycle helps you make informed decisions about when to upgrade or make other changes to your software. This product is governed by Microsoft's Modern Lifecycle Policy . The .NET and .NET Core support lifecycle offers support for each release. The length of time and degree of support vary based on a few qualifications. .NET and .NET Core are supported across several operating systems and versions. The .NET Supported OS Policy provides current details on operating systems support policies and versions. Customers can choose Long Term Support (LTS) releases or Standard Term Support (STS) releases. The quality of all releases is the same. The only difference is the length of support. LTS releases get free support and patches for three years. STS releases get free support and patches for two years. The following table tracks release and end of support dates for .NET and .NET Core versions. A new major release of .NET is published every year in November, enabling developers, the community, and businesses to plan their roadmaps. Even numbered releases are LTS releases that get free support and patches for three years. Odd numbered releases are STS releases that get free support and patches for two years. STS releases are supported for one year after a subsequent release. Releases happen every 12 months so the support period for STS is two years. items.body: SEOUL, Nov. 10 (Yonhap) -- Boy group Stray Kids has added 25 concerts in regions including North America and Europe for its ongoing world tour. The group announced on social media on Monday that it will perform on 25 additional nights, including April 24-25 in Yokohama, Japan, May 16 in Seattle, May 18 in Chicago, May 25 in Toronto, July 9 in Paris, July 13 in London and July 31 in Milan, Italy. This will bring the total scale of the "Run It" tour to 46 performances across 31 regions worldwide. The eight-piece group kicked off the tour with five sold-out shows at KSPO Dome in southern Seoul in July and August. The band's latest album "This & That" topped the Billboard 200 upon its release in August, making it the group's ninth No. 1 on the U.S. Billboard's main albums chart. The album has remained on the chart for 12 consecutive weeks, underlining the group's sustained popularity in the United States. Stray Kids has also captivated its international fans with its appearances at the Governors Ball Music Festival in New York, Rock in Rio in Brazil and its own "Stray City" music festival series across Latin America. items.body: Plus: ABC announces its midseason premiere lineup, which won’t include the new “Grey’s Anatomy” spinoff. And in larger Disney-owned television news, employees at the Mouse House are starting to feel the pressure from an impending restructuring. Surprise! While we were all distracted with the midterm results last week, it looks like Fox Corp. completed its $22 billion acquisition of Roku on Friday. Anyway, you know what acquisition deals mean: executive shakeups. Roku Media President Charlie Collier and Senior Vice President and General Counsel Chris Handman will not be joining Fox. Also on the outs: Tubi CEO Anjali Sud, who is taking a new role outside the company, and Robyn Peterson, who served as executive vice president of Fox-owned ad tech platform AdRise. Anthony Wood will be succeeded as Roku CEO by Mustafa Ozgen , who will also lead AdRise. Disney’s impending TV reorganization is starting to become real. In addition to another possible round of layoffs in January, Disney Entertainment Television is expected to undergo a massive restructuring under Chairman Debra OConnell, who took on the new role in March. Cable juggernaut Charter Communications is also planning a massive restructuring in an effort to save $2 billion over the next 18 months. The company reported $14.9 billion in revenue last quarter as a result of its merger with Spectrum, and a $2.4 billion loss stemming from a $6.3 billion franchise impairment charge. British TV producer Jack Bayles has been asked to step back from his current role as head of comedy at Various Artists Unlimited for reasons associated with the allegations against Russell Brand , who was convicted of rape and sexual assault last week. Various Artists is best known for producing “I May Destroy You,” Michaela Coel’s hit series about a writer who struggles with the aftermath of her own sexual assault. Lionsgate posted earnings for its second fiscal quarter on Thursday. Although the studio still suffered a slight net loss of $15.5 million, it exceeded analyst expectations by growing its overall revenue 41% year over year to $666.8 million. Lionsgate also announced that its massive film and TV IP library generated $1.04 billion over the last 12 months. items.headline: Digital Fairness Act trafia pod obrady Komisji w środę
items.summary: projekt ma wpisać limity manipulacyjnego designu, mechanik uzależniających i trudnych do anulowania subskrypcji w prawo konsumenckie, obejmując też podmioty, do których DSA nie dociera.
items.matters: dotknie każdego, kto sprzedaje subskrypcję lub prowadzi sklep w UE, a tekstu wciąż nie opublikowano.
items.body: The Commission's planning document for the meeting lists a consumer package covering a legislative act on digital fairness and a consumer enforcement initiative, and the document is indicative. MLex reported on Sept. 29 that the Commission had provisionally slotted the DFA for that meeting and that the schedule can change. Justice and Consumer Protection Commissioner Michael McGrath is due to carry the file . The proposal grows out of a 2024 fitness check of EU consumer law online. That review found that 97% of examined sites and apps used at least one dark pattern, and it estimated consumer harm at €7.9 billion (about $8.8 billion) a year. In a 2024 mission letter, Commission President Ursula von der Leyen asked McGrath to tackle dark patterns, influencer marketing , addictive design and profiling that exploits consumer vulnerabilities. Law firm CMS summarizes the Fitness Check as defining dark patterns as practices built into a digital interface's structure or design that push consumers toward decisions they would not otherwise make. No general EU definition exists in consumer law today. The likely headline areas are a formal definition and a list of banned practices, limits on features built to maximize time spent or compulsive spending, subscription cancellation, influencer marketing and personalization. CMS also lists loot boxes, in-game currencies, personalized pricing and protection of minors as likely topics. IAPP says McGrath's recent statements point to newer problems such as unfair live-event ticketing . None of this is confirmed until the text is published. Proposals raised during the review included a general ban on dark patterns and a "fairness by design" duty for traders. A general ban would put the burden on every trader's interface and sign-up flow; a list of specific banned practices would leave more room for designs the list does not name. The DSA already prohibits manipulative interface design on online platforms under Article 25 and sets duties for minors under Article 28. Legal analysts at Pinsent Masons note that micro and small enterprises and search engines fall outside the platform prohibition, along with individual traders who are not intermediaries, and that practices already covered by the Unfair Commercial Practices Directive or the GDPR are carved out. The DFA is widely seen as an attempt to close those gaps, and The European Post reports the Commission has indicated the Act will not single out specific actors or technologies. Addictive design is already being enforced under the DSA, but only against very large platforms.…
